title: TapAuth: Raspberry Pi NFC attendance and reservation kiosk with local-first registration
description:
Overview

TapAuth is a Raspberry Pi NFC attendance and reservation kiosk built for the Asia Pacific College School of Engineering AIRHub. The checkout folder name is irrelevant: the product, interface, and archived software are TapAuth.

Capabilities

  • Recognizes registered NFC cards from a durable local registry.
  • Records attendance through MySQL when available and reconciles after interruptions.
  • Supports 3D printing requests, teacher appointments, student management, and an optional Firebase copy with private and public data boundaries.
  • Retries a disconnected ACR122U reader and provides setup, update, synchronization, backup, and diagnostic scripts.

Install/Deploy

Deploy on Raspberry Pi OS with an ACR122U reader. Copy the environment template, enter private credentials, and run the provided setup script.

git clone https://github.com/devkyato/TapAuth.git
cd TapAuth
cp .env.example .env
nano .env
bash scripts/setup_raspberry_pi.sh

Quick start

After setup, open the kiosk locally and check the service.

sudo systemctl status airhub.service
# kiosk: http://127.0.0.1:5000/
# administration: http://127.0.0.1:5000/admin

Applications

  • School and laboratory attendance kiosks.
  • Local-first NFC registration and recognition.
  • Maker-space equipment, printing, and appointment workflows.

Limitations/status

TapAuth is a personal deployment-oriented project, not a hosted service or a source package. Real NFC operation requires supported hardware and Raspberry Pi configuration. MySQL is the main operational database; the local registry is a recognition fallback, and Firebase is optional.

Documentation

Start with the getting-started guide, then use the documentation and operations index.
